file.content: Todos

lines: /* [REQ-006] Priority shown as plain text, no colour, so only overdue is highlighted. */
.filters button { background: transparent; color: #1c1917; border: 1px solid #d6d3d1; padding: 0.35rem 0.75rem; }
+  <input type="search" class="search" data-testid="search-input" placeholder="Search todos" autocomplete="off" aria-label="Search todos">
+  var editingId = null;   // [REQ-007] id of the todo whose text is being edited
+  var rendering = false;  // [REQ-007] ignore blur caused by render removing the field
// [REQ-005] Within each group: high, then med, then low; same priority keeps insertion order.
+  // [REQ-007] Case-insensitive substring match; combines with the filter in render.
+        // [REQ-007] Enter or blur commits, Escape cancels.
+      if (t.id === id) { editingId = id; editDraft = t.text; }
+  // [REQ-007] Blank text keeps the old text instead of deleting the todo.

content.text:
I added both: double-click a todo's text to edit it in place (`todo-edit-input`), and a `search-input` box that combines with the filter. The script's syntax checks out, but I haven't tried either feature in a browser. If you save a blank edit, the todo keeps its old text; I chose that over deleting the todo.
Search is not saved and matches the literal text you type, spaces included.
